title: ₹80,000 Ka Phone Becha: Mobile Shop Wale Ko Kitna Mila?
description: Reasoning: every young Indian male has bought a phone and been upsold at the counter, so the hook is instantly relatable. The popcorn-over-the-movie reel on the multiplex shows our audience likes 'profit is hidden somewhere unexpected' stories. It also gives a practical takeaway for the viewer.
text:
HISAAB FACT SHEET: Mobile store margins (phone vs accessories vs protection plans)

**READ FIRST: the hook needs a fix**
- The hook as written ("margin on an ₹80,000 phone is smaller than on a ₹500 cover") is false in rupees. It is true per rupee sold.
- Arithmetic on the sourced figures (my calculation, not a sourced number): 6–7% of ₹80,000 is ₹4,800–5,600. A ₹500 cover at 40–70% margin is about ₹200–350.
- The same arithmetic on Apple's older 1.5–2% card-payment margin gives ₹1,200–1,600 on ₹80,000. That is still more rupees than the cover.
- Safer hook: "On every ₹100 of phone, the shop keeps about ₹4–7. On every ₹100 of back cover, it keeps ₹40–70." Say "per ₹100", not "per sale".
- No source I found gives retailer margin by phone price band. I could not build "by price band" bars. I can only give margin by brand and era (below).
- The price-band angle is also uncertain. One 2026 report says margin varies "depending on the model and price", but gives no split.

**1. PHONE MARGIN (the short bar)**
- Retailer margins currently run around 6–7%, depending on model and price. The All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA, 150,000+ members) is the source. [https://www.business-standard.com/industry/news/mobile-phone-sales-by-volume-plunge-30-35-in-may-as-prices-keep-rising-126061201152_1.html]
- Phone companies are now cutting retailer margins by 1–2% to soften price hikes. [same Business Standard URL]
- An earlier industry view (Ajay Sharma, ex-Micromax) put retail margins at about 4% on average. Distributors got 2.5–3%. [https://themobileindian.com/news/how-does-offline-mobile-distribution-work-in-india]
- Apple, older report from the iPhone X era: margin cut from 6.5% to 4.5% for large retailers. [https://retailnews.asia/apple-cuts-iphone-x-margins-indian-retailers]
- In that report, a card payment pushed the margin down to roughly 1.5–2%. The Sangeetha Mobiles MD said overheads were around 10%. [https://retailnews.asia/apple-cuts-iphone-x-margins-indian-retailers]
- The same era's report said Samsung and Xiaomi offered 12–15%, and Oppo and Vivo offered higher than usual. Treat the 12–15% as a dated and probably gross figure. [https://www.digit.in/news/mobile-phones/apple-cuts-iphone-x-margin-for-retailers-store-owners-pull-down-the-stock-38257.html]
- Backend schemes: brands pay extra margin for hitting targets, such as pushing one model or clearing old stock. The percentage varies by brand. The shop can pass some of it to the customer as a discount. [https://themobileindian.com/news/how-does-offline-mobile-distribution-work-in-india]
- Net profit is far thinner than margin. AIMRA says small mobile retailers run on net profit margins below 1.5%. [https://www.communicationstoday.co.in/mobile-retailers-warn-store-closures-post-diwali-over-proposed-mdr/]
- A blog claim of 10–15% on smartphones looks like a gross-margin overstatement against the 4–7% above. Don't use it. [https://getswipe.in/blog/article/how-to-start-mobile-shop-business]

**2. ACCESSORY MARGIN (the tall bar)**
- Covers 40–70% and tempered glass 50–80%. These are blog estimates for accessory shops. [https://www.thebusinessunbox.com/mobile-accessories-shop-business-plan/]
- Another guide gives covers 40–60% and tempered glass 50–70%. [https://www.vyapargrow.com/mobile-accessories-shop-business/]
- Chargers and cables 20–50%. Earphones 25–60%. [https://www.thebusinessunbox.com/mobile-accessories-shop-business-plan/]
- Fancy back cover example: cost ₹40–60, sells ₹150–250. That is a 200–300% markup, not margin. [https://thebandhu.com/mobile-shop-business-plan-hindi/]
- Tempered glass example: wholesale ₹60, retail ₹199–299, quoted as 70–80% margin. This is a weak, supplier-style source. [https://www.alibaba.com/product-insights/mobile-tempered-glass-wholesale-price-in-india.html]
- Another Delhi wholesaler example: buy at ₹27.60, sell at ₹90–100. It claims ₹30,000+ monthly profit on 500 pieces. That is a seller's marketing claim. [https://www.karolbaghtemperedglass.com/uncategorized/mobile-tempered-glass-wholesale-price-india-2025/]
- Wholesale-side view: new flagship phones give 3–8%. Accessories give 15–35%. Branded audio gives 12–22%. [https://www.solgroup.net/mobile-distributors-electronics-fmcg-expansion/]
- Sourcing: Delhi is India's tempered glass hub, and shop owners from across India buy there. [https://mobileglassfactory.com/]
- Insider fact: glass is the easiest add-on because every phone sale is a chance to ask for it. Fitting it in-store is part of the pitch. [https://mobileglassfactory.com/]
- Caveat: all accessory margin figures are from blogs and suppliers, not audited. Market size claimed: over ₹25,000 crore a year (a supplier's claim). [https://www.karolbaghtemperedglass.com/uncategorized/mobile-tempered-glass-wholesale-price-india-2025/]

**3. PROTECTION PLAN MARGIN (the surprise bar)**
- Plan prices run 1–4% of device price per year of cover. [https://assurify.in/protection-plans/]
- Example quotes from Assurify: ₹899 for 1-year extended warranty on a ₹64,999 phone (1.4%). ₹2,499 for 2-year SmartShield on a ₹74,999 phone (3.3%). [https://assurify.in/protection-plans/]
- Commission on offer: up to 35% for retailers selling plans at the billing counter. [https://merchant.assurify.in/]
- The same page lists extended warranty at up to 30%. [https://merchant.assurify.in/]
- Real-store example from Assurify's dashboard: 138 plans in a month earned about ₹42,900 on ₹4,29,000 of plan sales. That is about 10% of plan value (my arithmetic). [https://assurify.in/answers/how-retailers-sell-extended-warranty/]
- The same page lists "commission" examples of ₹899 (flagship phone plan) and ₹249 (mid-range phone plan). These ₹899 figures clash with the ₹899 premium above. Confirm before scripting, or use only the 138-plan example. [https://assurify.in/answers/how-retailers-sell-extended-warranty/]
- Cost to the shop: no stock, no deposit, no fulfilment. Commission is paid weekly into the store's bank account. [https://assurify.in/answers/how-retailers-sell-extended-warranty/]
- This is one provider's pitch to retailers. Other providers and brand plans pay differently, and I found no neutral commission data.
- Brand plans: Oppo charges a ₹499 processing fee under its screen protection plan. [https://www.oppo.com/in/store/contents/legal/oppo-protection-plan-terms-and-conditions/]
- Samsung Care+ offers extended warranty (1 year), screen-only protection (2 years) and combined cover (2 years). Damage plans must be bought within 15 days of purchase. [https://www.samsung.com/in/offer/samsung-care-plus/mobile/]

**Insider facts on plans (customer-facing "I never knew")**
- Extended warranty cover starts only after the manufacturer's warranty ends. A 1-year plan bought with a phone that already has a 1-year brand warranty may pay nothing in year one. [https://righttoinformation.wiki/extended-warranty-mis-sold-refund-cancellation-india]
- A protection plan is a separate paid contract, not a condition of sale. You can refuse it and still buy the phone. [https://righttoinformation.wiki/extended-warranty-mis-sold-refund-cancellation-india]
- Many retailer and brand plans are plain service contracts with no insurer behind them. Some IRDAI-registered insurers do sell regulated extended warranty with a policy wording and a UIN. [https://righttoinformation.wiki/extended-warranty-mis-sold-refund-cancellation-india]
- Screen cracks and spills are usually a separate damage-protection product. [same URL]

**4. DISTRIBUTOR CREDIT AND STOCK FINANCING**
- Chain: brand to distributor to retailer. Large chains like Croma, Reliance Digital and Vijay Sales are billed directly by brands, with no distributor. [https://themobileindian.com/news/how-does-offline-mobile-distribution-work-in-india]
- Distributors typically extend only 15–30 days of credit to electronics retailers. [https://www.indifi.com/blog/business-loan-for-mobile-or-electronics-shop/]
